newsitem.title: ITALY: Albania crisis shows flaws in EU policy, Dini says.
newsitem.headline: Albania crisis shows flaws in EU policy, Dini says.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Saturday unrest in Albania had shown the European Union's lack of preparation for crises on its doorstep and said it should be able to move quickly and even use force in such cases.

"The Albanian crisis is a classic European crisis of the post-Cold War era -- too far from the United States for the U.S. to take an immediate interest, too close to Europe for us to ignore it," Dini said in a speech in Venice.

"It is also evidence of inadequate analysis and planning. The European Union must equip itself adequately in this respect and with the means to intervene rapidly, including the use of force," he said.

Dini, addressing an Anglo-Italian seminar on the role of Britain and Italy in Europe, was speaking after Italy mounted its second mission within a week to evacuate citizens from the troubled southern Albanian port of Vlore.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman said more than 20 people had been evacuated on Saturday. On Monday, Italy brought 35 people back by helicopter from Vlore, a flashpoint in southern Albania which is gripped by an armed insurrection.

Dini said the European Union should be able to bring "political influence, military power and economic assistance to bear" in its foreign policy and should take foreign policy decisions by majority, not unanimity.
Britain is opposed to use of majority voting that could curtail the national veto.

"Can we really rely on a mechanism that risks being no different, in its decision-making, from the League of Nations?" Can the opposition of one country be allowed to paralyse the whole Union?" Dini asked.
"Without an appropriately far-sighted policy, Europe may not be able to prevent new and uncontrolled forms of nomadism throughout our continent," he said.
